protobuf-java-4.34.1.jar: CVE-2026-0994 is a false positive. The vulnerability is in the Python protobuf library's json_format.ParseDict() function — specifically a recursion-depth counter bug in Python's json_format.py. That code does not exist in the Java implementation. The NVD CPE cpe:/a:google:protobuf is language-agnostic and incorrectly matches the Java artifact. The fix versions cited (5.29.6, 6.33.5) are Python package versions; there is no corresponding Java fix because there is no vulnerability in the Java library. Added: 2026-04-23

httpcore-4.4.16.jar: CVE-2026-54399 and CVE-2026-54428 are false positives on the httpcore 4.x line. Both vulnerabilities are HTTP/2 issues in the HttpComponents Core 5.x codebase (the HPackDecoder / HTTP/2 header handling in httpcore5 / httpcore5-h2), fixed in 5.4.2. The httpcore 4.x line does not contain that HTTP/2 code and is not affected. The NVD CPE cpe:/a:apache:httpcomponents_core uses an upper-bound-only range ("up to and including 5.4.2"), so dependency-check numerically matches 4.4.16 (<= 5.4.2) on the shared CPE. 4.4.16 is the terminal 4.x release, so there is no newer 4.x to upgrade to; it is pulled in transitively by izgw-core's OCSP revocation code, which references only a couple of string constants from the 4.x jars. The 5.x artifacts (httpcore5/httpcore5-h2) already resolve to a fixed version (>= 5.4.3). Added: 2026-07-07

kotlin-stdlib-1.9.25.jar: CVE-2026-53914 is not exploitable in this service. The vulnerability is a BUILD-TIME issue in Kotlin's build cache metadata (unsafe deserialization, CWE-502), only reachable when compiling Kotlin with Kotlin's build tooling. izgw-transform is a Maven/Java service that runs no Kotlin compiler and no Kotlin build cache, so the vulnerable code path is not present at runtime. kotlin-stdlib is only on the classpath transitively (via okio/okhttp under org.hl7.fhir.utilities); a representative VXU^V04 -> FHIR conversion loaded 0 kotlin and 0 okhttp classes.
MATCH NOTE: kotlin-stdlib is a Gradle-built jar with no embedded META-INF/maven pom.properties, so the CI scan (dependency-check GitHub Action scanning the assembled fat jar) derives no Maven packageUrl for it and identifies it only by cpe:/a:jetbrains:kotlin. A packageUrl suppression therefore does not match; this rule matches by filePath (the nested jar filename), which works in both the fat-jar and Maven-plugin scans.
Scanner shows the inflated NVD 9.8 auto-score; JetBrains (CNA) rates it 6.7 Medium (AV:L/AC:H/PR:H). Fixed in Kotlin 2.4.20, not yet GA (betas only as of 2026-07-28). TEMPORARY: remove once Kotlin 2.4.20 GA is pinned via kotlin-bom in izgw-bom. Added: 2026-07-28 (IGDD-3141)

tomcat-embed-core: CVE-2026-66299 is a false positive for embedded Tomcat usage. The vulnerability is an unbounded buffer for undelivered messages in the WebSocket chat example web application bundled with the full Apache Tomcat distribution, allowing a slow client to exhaust memory. Apache's own advisory states users who removed the examples web application are not affected. Our use of tomcat-embed does not include the examples web application - this is Spring Boot's embedded Tomcat (tomcat-embed-core/-el/-websocket only, pulled in via izgw-bom's tomcat.version property), which never bundles the examples webapp in the first place. Confirmed as a known false-positive pattern on the Apache Tomcat security mailing list thread for this CVE.
Fixed versions (11.0.25 / 10.1.58 / 9.0.121) had not been released as of this writing - confirmed tomcat-embed-core 10.1.58 does not yet exist on Maven Central (still under development). Revisit once 10.1.58 ships; this suppression may become unnecessary (harmless if left in place - it will simply stop matching). Added: 2026-08-08 (IGDD-3254)
